title: Your Phone System Just Got a Lot More Expensive (And Nobody's Talking About It)
excerpt: VoIP pricing is quietly climbing across the board in 2026, and if you haven't shopped around lately, you might be overpaying without even knowing it.

content.text: So I've been digging through the VoIP pricing landscape this morning, and okay—this is the kind of thing that doesn't make headlines but absolutely should matter to you. Pretty much every major VoIP provider has either raised prices, restructured their plans, or added sneaky fees for things that used to be included. And here's the thing: most small business owners don't realize they're paying more because they just never go back and check.

The VoIP market has gotten really competitive, which sounds great, but it's actually pushing providers to do something weird with their pricing. Instead of just charging more upfront—which you'd notice—they're building out bigger "base" plans with all these features bundled in, then charging per-user add-ons for things like AI receptionists, advanced call analytics, or premium support. It's a smart business move. For them. For you? It means your monthly bill can creep up 30–40% without you realizing what happened.

items: Base plans are getting pricier across the board (we're talking $25–$35+ per user per month for solid options)
Add-ons that used to be included now cost extra—AI features, call recording quality tiers, advanced reporting
Some providers are pushing you toward their "full stack" solutions (phone + CRM + customer service automation), which sounds great until your bill doubles

content.text: The real kicker: if you signed up 2–3 years ago and haven't reviewed your plan since, you could easily be paying 40–50% more than a new customer signing up for the exact same features today.
Why This Matters to You (Right Now)

Look, your phone system is important, but it's probably not something you think about every month. Which means you're either on autopilot with your current provider, or you're trying to compare three different providers and getting totally confused by all the options. Either way, you're leaving money on the table. For a 10–20 person team, that could be an extra $100–300 a month you don't need to be spending.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: Here's what I'd do if I were you: pull up your last three VoIP invoices right now. Actually look at what you're paying for. Then spend 20 minutes pricing out 2–3 alternatives (and don't just look at the base price—add up what you'd actually use). I'm betting you'll find at least one option that covers everything you need for less. Seriously, do this today. It's the easiest money you'll save all quarter.
The Hidden Stuff Nobody Tells You

The providers aren't being sketchy—it's just how the industry works now. But here's what to actually watch for when you're comparing: per-minute charges for international or long-distance calls, premium support tiers that sound optional until something breaks, call recording storage (it adds up fast), and those "AI features" that sound cheap until you realize they're metered or have overage fees. Read the fine print. Boring, I know. Worth it? Absolutely.
